title: Verifier‑Assisted versus LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We measured whether integrating a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier with a bounded automated repair budget increases the fraction of intent‑driven network‑change proposals that pass semantic validation compared with accepting a single LLM candidate. In a preregistered paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per difficulty stratum: low/medium/high) using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic NetOps validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Each paired intent produced one shared_initial generation that was evaluated under two conditions: baseline (accept single shot) and guarded (deterministic validation and ≤1 automated repair). Outcomes: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.9966667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00,0.01] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). Under the supplied synthetic suite and repair budget the single‑shot generator was near ceiling, limiting observable deterministic rescue. We archive preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts and interpret results with respect to estimand conditioning, validator coverage, repair budget, and operational deployment policies.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being applied to NetOps tasks such as intent→configuration translation, configuration synthesis, and automated repair. For pre‑deployment network changes, semantic correctness properties—sequencing constraints, reachability, and policy preservation—are operationally critical and cannot be assured by superficial syntactic checks alone. A common engineering pattern is to pair generative models with deterministic validators and bounded automated repair (generate→validate→repair) to reduce operational risk. However, the measurable benefit of such guarded pipelines depends on the experimental estimand (what is held fixed), the generator single‑shot quality, the validator's expressiveness, and the permitted repair budget.

We preregistered a paired experiment (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) that isolates the deterministic rescue achievable when the same single LLM candidate is evaluated under two treatments. For each intent the pipeline produced exactly one shared_initial candidate using gpt-5-mini and compared: (a) baseline — accept the single candidate without repair, and (b) guarded — run a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and allow at most one automated repair which itself is re‑validated. The primary research question: does adding a deterministic verifier plus at most one automated repair increase the probability that a single LLM candidate passes semantic pre‑deployment validation compared with accepting that same candidate without repair?

Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired evaluation isolating deterministic rescue under a shared_initial estimand; (2) a complete execution and analysis bundle including validator traces and the single automated repair transcript; (3) an evidence‑grounded interpretation of estimator conditioning, ceiling effects, and operational implications for NetOps pipelines.
sections.related_work:
Recent surveys and systems document active application of LLMs to NetOps tasks including intent‑to‑configuration translation, template synthesis, protocol test generation, and repair [1–6]. Tool‑augmented architectures (planner‑centric frameworks, ReAct‑style pipelines) enable LLMs to call external validators and simulators to decompose multi‑step workflows [7,8]; empirical reports indicate that deterministic checks and generate→validate→repair scaffolds can improve surface correctness metrics relative to unconstrained generation, but gains depend on validator expressiveness and task distribution [3,4].

Two methodological themes motivate our design. First, many prior evaluations conflate verifier benefits with resampling or verifier‑guided regeneration; this obscures the deterministic rescue attributable to post‑generation checking alone [4,9]. Second, public NetOps benchmarks often emphasize syntactic or template correctness rather than semantics (reachability, sequencing, policy preservation), limiting operational generality of claims [10,11]. Hybrid repair approaches that combine symbolic fault localization with generative repair show promise but succeed variably across fault classes and verifier coverage [12,3]. Detection and mitigation work on hallucinations and safety nets (entropy/semantic detectors, retrieval augmentation, self‑reflection) further influences practical pipeline design [13,14]. Our study positions itself within these threads by fixing the shared_initial estimand to bound model‑call budgets and isolate verifier/repair effects.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered the confirmatory design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) and froze the primary estimand: the absolute paired difference in the unflagged verifier‑pass proportion (guarded − baseline) on N = 300 paired intents after the prespecified inclusion/exclusion rules. The preregistration specified a paired analysis executor, contingency reporting, an exact two‑sided McNemar test for discordant pairs, and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (seed = 1729, B = 10000). An optional calibration pilot (n = 60) for discordance estimation was included in the registration but not executed prior to the main run; no post‑registration design changes were made.

Task generation and stratification. Tasks were deterministically generated into a synthetic topology suite stratified into three difficulty strata (low/medium/high) with 100 paired intents per stratum in the confirmatory run. Each task encoded the natural‑language intent, initial and expected final states, required sequencing constraints (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields), preserve_unspecified_state invariants, and protected_interfaces. Difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count) determined stratum membership.

Shared_initial protocol and model configuration. To isolate deterministic validator/repair rescue from generator resampling effects we implemented a shared_initial estimand: for each pair the pipeline produced exactly one shared_initial candidate that was reused verbatim for both conditions. The declared generator used for shared_initial production was gpt-5-mini (requested_model = "gpt-5-mini"); maximal output tokens and other operational parameters were fixed prior to execution. Reusing the same candidate across conditions prevents differences due to independent model draws and measures only deterministic validation and bounded repair applied to identical output.

Validator and repair operator. Semantic evaluation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementing the preregistered full_intent_constraint_validation rule: sequencing invariants, required_command_count, preservation of unspecified state, topology reachability invariants encoded by the suite, and forbidden‑template protections. Scoring is binary: an unflagged candidate is a pass for the estimand. The guarded pipeline permitted at most one automated repair attempt (repair budget ≤ 1). The repair operator is a constrained edit routine limited to localized sequencing and insertion edits (e.g., inserting a missing 'admin down' before a VLAN/MTU change) and is applied only if the validator flags the shared_initial candidate; repaired candidates are re‑validated deterministically.

Contamination controls and missingness rules. The preregistration required negative controls and deterministic contamination detection; a pair was excluded from confirmatory analysis only if both pipeline calls failed due to provider/infrastructure outage. Pairs with single‑call failures were retained under the executor policy; sensitivity analyses treating single failures as failures were preplanned. The missingness plan required logging all provider/API failures; no dual‑call outages occurred in the confirmatory run.

Execution and audit. The run executed under an adapter enforcing the shared_initial protocol and repair budget. Key execution summary values (reported in Results) are: planned_episode_count = 600, completed_episode_count = 600, complete_pair_count = 300, and model_calls_used = 301 (300 shared_initial generations plus one repair invocation). Execution instrumentation audited stage counts to confirm that the same shared_initial candidate was used across conditions and that the repair stage was invoked only when the validator flagged a candidate.

Analysis. The preregistered confirmatory analysis computed the 2×2 paired contingency (n11,n10,n01,n00), the absolute paired difference, an exact two‑sided McNemar test on discordant counts, and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (seed = 1729, B = 10000). Secondary and stratum tests were treated as exploratory and subject to multiplicity control where reported. All analysis code and inputs were archived to permit deterministic re‑execution.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and integrity. The adapter completed the confirmatory run as preregistered with completed_episode_count = 600, yielding complete_pair_count = 300 paired observations under the shared_initial protocol and model_calls_used = 301. Audit stage counts indicate 300 shared_initial generations and a single repair invocation. No pairs were excluded under the prespecified rules and no provider/infrastructure dual‑call outages occurred.

Primary confirmatory outcomes. Binary scoring produced baseline_success_count = 299 and guarded_success_count = 300: baseline = 299/300 (0.9966667) and guarded = 300/300 (1.0). The paired contingency table is n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test on discordant counts returned p = 1.0. The absolute paired improvement (guarded − baseline) equals 0.0033333. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (seed = 1729, B = 10000) is [0.00, 0.01]. Given the minimal discordance (m = 1), the exact test has low sensitivity to small absolute differences; the bootstrap CI bounds the plausible absolute improvement to at most one percentage point under the registered estimand and suite.

Per‑stratum diagnostics and repair trace. Per‑stratum tallies were: low baseline = 100/100 and guarded = 100/100; medium baseline = 100/100 and guarded = 100/100; high baseline = 99/100 and guarded = 100/100. The single discordant case occurred in the high stratum. Validator diagnostics attribute the initial failure to a sequencing omission (a required 'admin down' before a VLAN/MTU change). The constrained repair operator applied a single localized insertion of the missing sequencing command; on revalidation the corrected candidate passed deterministically. Thus the solitary rescue required one repair invocation and no additional model draws beyond the recorded repair stage.

Contamination and missingness. Preplanned contamination checks and negative controls raised no flags in the main run. The missingness summary reports zero failed or unscorable episodes and zero excluded pairs under preregistered rules.

Operational cost. The guarded pipeline's deterministic rescue required a single additional repair stage call across 300 pairs (model_calls_used = 301), demonstrating that in this run bounded automated repair imposed minimal extra model‑call cost. The observed repair_stage_count = 1 quantifies the low marginal model cost for deterministic rescue under the chosen edit operator and repair budget.

Statistical interpretation. The inferential outcome (p = 1.0) primarily reflects the paucity of discordant pairs under the shared_initial estimand and chosen synthetic suite. Exact McNemar inference depends on n10 and n01; with n10 = 1 and n01 = 0 a two‑sided exact p equals 1.0, indicating no statistically detectable difference under conventional two‑sided testing in this sample. The paired bootstrap CI provides a complementary bound for effect size. These inferential statements apply strictly to the shared_initial conditioning (one LLM draw reused across conditions), the limited repair budget (≤1 edit), the synthetic task distribution, and the declared generator and validator.
sections.discussion:
Estimand conditioning and operational alignment. The shared_initial estimand corresponds to operational policies that constrain model calls for cost, latency, or governance reasons; under that policy the guarded pipeline measures only deterministic validator and bounded repair rescue applied to the same candidate. Workflows that permit resampling, verifier‑guided regeneration, or interactive steering change the estimand and typically increase achievable success rates by exploiting generator variance; such workflows should be evaluated under a different preregistered design.

Ceiling effects and the omitted pilot. The preregistration aimed to detect a 10 percentage‑point absolute improvement with power ≈0.8 after a pilot to estimate discordance. The optional pilot was not executed; the main run encountered a near‑ceiling baseline (299/300), producing minimal discordance (m = 1) and reduced power to detect small absolute differences. This practical outcome highlights the value of small calibration pilots when generator performance may approach ceiling on selected suites.

Validator coverage and failure‑mode dependence. The observed single failure mode was a sequencing omission; other classes (reachability violations, forbidden ACL removal) were not observed at scale on this synthetic suite. The marginal utility of a guarded pipeline therefore depends on (a) the deployment distribution of failure modes and (b) validator expressiveness: richer validators that detect reachability or ACL semantics may increase observable rescue rates, while operator policies that disallow automated edits limit guarded pipelines to detection and escalation.

Repair budget and operator design. We intentionally limited automated repair to a single constrained edit to measure bounded deterministic rescue. Iterative repair, more powerful edit operators, or verifier‑guided regeneration would increase rescue opportunities but address a different estimand and resource tradeoff. The archived repair trace from the rescued episode can inform permitted edit‑operator design in production pipelines.

Implications for NetOps CI/CD. Organizations must align evaluation estimands with operational choices. If pipelines allow multiple model calls, evaluations should permit resampling and interactive steering. If model calls are tightly budgeted, the shared_initial estimand provides an operationally meaningful bound for deterministic verifier/repair rescue applied to a single candidate. In this run bounded repair produced a deterministic rescue at very low additional model cost for a single hard example.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired comparison on 300 synthetic NetOps intents using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 under a shared_initial estimand, baseline single‑shot generation produced 299/300 unflagged verifier passes and the guarded pipeline 300/300. The absolute paired improvement was 0.00333 (exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.01]). Deterministic validator+repair rescued a single sequencing omission under the bounded repair budget. The near‑ceiling baseline limited inferential sensitivity to small absolute improvements under the shared_initial estimand. Full preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts are archived to support reproducibility and targeted follow‑ups that vary estimand conditioning, model strength, task distribution, or repair budget.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated by the preregistered deterministic generator; real‑world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase verifier marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or richer/diverse validators.

Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing limited discordance and reduced power to detect small absolute improvements relative to larger pre‑specified targets.
Pilot not executed: the preregistered pilot intended for discordance estimation and power calibration was not run; no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed.

Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit that would arise from allowing independent alternative LLM candidates per condition (resampling or iterative generation).
Repair budget: the guarded condition permitted at most one automated repair per pair; larger or iterative repair strategies may yield different outcomes.
